message.content:
Below is a quick “recipe” you can copy‑paste into your terminal (or adapt for PowerShell / Python) to pull up to ten file reports that have communicated with the IP **12.234.56.126** via VirusTotal’s v3 REST API.

> ⚠️ **Do NOT post your real API key anywhere public!**  
> Keep `my_api` secret – replace it with your own key when you run the commands below.

---

### 1️⃣ One‑liner with *curl*

```bash
curl -s \
     --request GET \
     --url "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/12.234.56.126/files?limit=10&cursor=pointer" \
     --header "x-apikey: my_api"
```

*Explanation:*  

| Part | What it does |
|------|--------------|
| `--request GET` | Explicitly tells curl we’re doing a GET request. |
| URL path `/ip_addresses/<IP>/files` | Endpoint that lists all files seen contacting that IP. |
| Query params `?limit=10&cursor=pointer` | Ask for at most 10 results (`limit`) and start after whatever record ID is stored in `pointer`. Replace `"pointer"` with the value returned in the previous page’s response if you want to paginate further. |
| Header `x-apikey:` | Your personal VT API key. |

If everything goes well you’ll receive a JSON blob containing metadata for each matching file (hashes, first/last observed dates, detection stats, etc.).

---

### 2️⃣ Using *PowerShell* (Windows)

```powershell
$headers   = @{ "x-apikey"="my_api" }
$url       = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/12.234.56.126/files?limit=10&cursor=pointer"

Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $url -Headers $headers -Method Get
```

Same logic—just wrapped in PowerShell cmdlets.

---

### 3️⃣ Quick Python snippet

```python
import requests

API_KEY = "my_api"
BASE_URL = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/"
IP_ADDR  = "12.234.56.126"
LIMIT    = 10          # maximum per request
CURSOR   = "pointer"   # change once you hit next_page_cursor

endpoint = f"{BASE_URL}/ip_addresses/{IP_ADDR}/files"
params   = {"limit": LIMIT, "cursor": CURSOR}
headers  = {"x-apikey": API_KEY}

resp = requests.get(endpoint, headers=headers, params=params)
print(resp.json())
```

Just paste that into a `.py` file, install `requests` (`pip install requests`), then run it.

---

#### 📌 Things to keep in mind

| Topic | Why it matters |
|-------|----------------|
| **Rate limiting** | Free tier → ~4 req/minute. If you exceed, you’ll see HTTP 429 responses. |
| **Pagination** | Each successful call returns a field called `links.next.cursor`. Use that value instead of `"pointer"` to fetch subsequent pages. |
| **Data privacy** | File hashes may belong to users who haven’t consented to sharing. Treat the output responsibly. |
| **Error handling** | A non‑200 status means something went wrong (bad key, bad IP, network issue…). Inspect `response.status_code` & `response.text`. |

That’s basically all you need to pull those records yourself. Happy hunting!
